books.title: Redemption: The Story of a Woman
books.line: What breaks is not the end of the story.
books.summary: A woman's story, told plainly and without flinching: the seasons that undo us, and the grace that meets a woman precisely there.
books.signedCopies: By request via email; no price set yet
coverSymbols: Where her face should be, a rose in full bloom: beauty and identity restored, rising out of suffering rather than apart from it.
Barbed stems cross her back like bindings: the pain, shame and circumstance a woman can find herself wrapped in.
Transformation is already in the air, even while the thorns remain.
She kneels in black water, low but not lost: a woman at the turning point of her story.

books.title: Redemptions Journey
books.titleNote: Styled without an apostrophe, as on the published cover
books.line: Being set free is the beginning. Learning to walk free is the journey.
books.summary: Everything that comes after the rescue: the daily, deliberate work of healing, growing and becoming.
books.signedCopies: By request via email; no price set yet
coverSymbols: Deep green, the colour of living things: no longer kneeling, but mid-stride.
The thorns that bound her are in her hands and snapping at her wrists: freedom seized and walked in.
The thicket that imprisoned her erupts in flower: the past is not erased; it is redeemed.
Bright against the dark: defined not by what held her, but by where she is going.

readingCircleQuestions: What does "redemption" mean to you, and did the book change that definition?
The covers show a woman bound by vines. What are the "thorns" women carry most quietly, and why do they go unspoken?
Why does change so often arrive as a process rather than an event? Where have you seen that in your own life?
What sustains belief when circumstances give it nothing to stand on?
In the second cover, the imprisoning vines burst into flower. What might it mean for a painful past to be redeemed rather than erased?
What is one practice, daily, unglamorous, faithful, that helps a person live out a new chapter?

items: Where can I buy Laketha's books?
Both books are on Amazon in paperback and Kindle. Signed copies are available by request; write to hello@lakethahicks.com.
Which book should I read first?
Start with Redemption: The Story of a Woman (2020), then Redemptions Journey (2022). Either stands alone, but together they trace the full arc from breaking to blooming.
Are the two books a series?
Yes. Book One tells the story; Book Two walks it out.
Can our book club or group read them together?
Please do. Discussion questions are free on the books page, and Laketha welcomes invitations to visit reading circles.
How can I contact Laketha about her books?
Use the contact page or write to hello@lakethahicks.com.
